investigation: Pygmy Dipole Resonance (PDR) Cross-Mass Transferability Breakdown and Isoscalar-Isovector Splitting
description: Comprehensive evaluation of low-energy E1 strength, neutron skin scaling, probe selectivity bifurcation ((alpha,alpha') vs (gamma,gamma')), and collective vs single-particle breakdown limits across 68Ni, 112-124Sn, and 208Pb.

probe_bifurcation.note: Relativistic heavy-ion Coulomb excitation only; no alpha probe contrast available

boundary_1_collective_to_single_particle.mechanism: In heavy 208Pb, high level density and multiple valence shells generate coherent superposition across >10 1p-1h configurations (dominant fraction < 15%). In medium-mass 68Ni across the N=40 subshell gap, the PDR collapses into an incoherent single-particle transition (nu 2p1/2 -> 3s1/2 carries 68% of strength). Direct transfer of 'collective skin vibration' to A~60 fails completely.
boundary_1_collective_to_single_particle.failure_signature: Absence of QRPA collective phase coherence; sharp sensitivity to single-particle orbital placement.

boundary_2_skinless_e1_background.mechanism: While 124Sn exhibits enhanced PDR strength (0.76 e2 fm2, 1.22% TRK) correlating with a thick neutron skin (0.19 fm), 112Sn has virtually no neutron skin (0.01 fm) yet still displays significant low-lying E1 strength (0.38 e2 fm2, 0.72% TRK). A naive linear extrapolation E1 ~ delta_r_np predicts zero strength, failing due to shell core-polarization and non-resonant single-particle transitions.
boundary_2_skinless_e1_background.failure_signature: Non-zero intercept in B(E1) vs neutron skin thickness plot.

boundary_3_probe_selectivity_bifurcation.mechanism: The low-lying 1- spectrum in 120,124Sn and 208Pb bifurcates into two distinct regimes across the neutron separation threshold S_n: states below S_n feature in-phase neutron-proton interior motion with surface neutron excess, yielding high (alpha,alpha') cross-sections; states above S_n belong to the isovector GDR tail with out-of-phase interior motion, yielding near-zero (alpha,alpha') cross-sections (a 15.0-fold contrast). In 68Ni, Coulomb excitation at relativistic speeds excites both simultaneously without hadronic surface filtering.
boundary_3_probe_selectivity_bifurcation.failure_signature: Single-probe measurements cannot determine PDR collectivity without paired hadronic-electromagnetic forward-angle scattering.
